title: A fibre-regular germ with nonzero differential at a separable smooth point
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, $k=\kappa(s)$ and $L=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $x_s$ be the point over $x$ in $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume $x_s$ is closed, $L/k$ is finite-dimensional and separable algebraic [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and $\dim_{x_s}X_s=d\geq1$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then there are affine open neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $s$, with $f(W)\subseteq V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that $B\to A$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\Omega_{A/B}$ is free of rank $d$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $C=k\otimes_B A$, with multiplication $(\lambda\otimes a)(\mu\otimes b)=\lambda\mu\otimes ab$, and let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ correspond to $x_s$ under $W_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Then $C$ is a smooth finite-type $k$-algebra, and $R=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is canonically $\mathcal O_{X_s,x_s}$, with residue field $L$. It is a regular local ring and an integral domain [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Writing $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal, after choosing a basis of $\Omega_{A/B}$ there are induced $L$-linear identifications
$$E:=\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R L\cong\Omega_{A/B}\otimes_A L\cong L^d\cong\Omega^1_{X/S,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}L$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], compatible with the universal derivations. The map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to E$, $b\bmod\mathfrak m^2\mapsto db\otimes1$, is surjective. There exists a germ $h\in\mathfrak m_x\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$ whose fibre image $\bar h\in\mathfrak m$ has $d\bar h\otimes1\ne0$ in $E$; under these identifications this is the image of $dh$ in the relative differential fibre at $x$. Multiplication by $\bar h$ on $R$ is injective. Here stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and regular local includes Noetherian as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 057D, lemma-slice-smooth-once, proof: fibre local ring, conormal sequence and lifting the germ; Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, positive-dimensional case: finite separable residue differentials vanish.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] to $f,x$ to obtain $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $x\in W$, $f(W)\subset V$, and $\Omega_{A/B}$ free of rank $d$. Its dimension is the dimension of the same fibre at $x_s$, namely the assumed $d$. The restriction $W\to V$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a); [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] therefore makes $B\to A$ a smooth ring map. Fix a basis of $\Omega_{A/B}$.

source.place: Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free; Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize, affine restriction and ring criterion; agreement with formal smoothness: more-morphisms.tex, Tag 02H6.

proof.text: The finite presentation furnished by smoothness allows [lem-trf-affine-fibre-point-dimension] to identify the inverse image $W_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $C=k\otimes_B A$, and $x_s$ with the prime $\mathfrak q$. Its tensor algebra is precisely the one with the multiplication in the statement; the chart lemma also gives that $C$ is finite type over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $C_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,x_s}$. Put $T=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], the structural map $T\to R=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is the surjection $T\to T/J$, where $J=\mathfrak m_sT$. The stalk map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to T$ is local, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$. Thus $R$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x/J$, and $R/\mathfrak m=T/\mathfrak m_x=L$, with the structural residue maps.

source.place: Tags 01JQ and 01JR, lemma-fibre-product-affines and lemma-open-fibre-product; Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6); Tag 0HA1, lemma-local-ring-fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1) to $B\to A$ and $B\to k$. It gives that $k\to C=k\otimes_B A$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], the localization $R=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local (in particular Noetherian). By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $R$ is an integral domain. None of these applications requires $S$ to be Noetherian or $k$ to be perfect.

source.place: Tag 00T4, lemma-base-change-smooth; Tag 00TT, lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, final assertion; Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], successively,
$\Omega_{C/k}\cong C\otimes_A\Omega_{A/B}$ and $\Omega_{R/k}\cong R\otimes_C\Omega_{C/k}$. Tensor with $L$ to obtain $E\cong L\otimes_A\Omega_{A/B}\cong L^d$, using the chosen basis. The first two isomorphisms send $1\otimes da$ to $d(1\otimes a)$ and $dc/u$ to $u^{-1}d(c/1)$. For the other end of the claimed chain, [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identifies the differential sheaf on $W$ with the sheaf associated to $\Omega_{A/B}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identifies its stalk at $x$ with $(\Omega_{A/B})_{\mathfrak p}$, where $\mathfrak p\subset A$ represents $x$. Tensoring this stalk with $L$ again gives $\Omega_{A/B}\otimes_A L$. Reorder the tensors using $l\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes l$. All maps respect derivations: for a germ $h=a/t$ ($t\notin\mathfrak p$), both routes send its differential to $t^{-1}da-a t^{-2}dt$ evaluated in $L$. This follows by differentiating $t t^{-1}=1$ and then $a t^{-1}$; it also proves compatibility for every germ, rather than just for sections of $A$.

source.place: Tags 00RV and 00RT, lemma-differentials-base-change and lemma-differentials-localize; morphisms.tex Tag 01UT, lemma-differentials-affine; schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (7).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $k\to R$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m$, with quotient $L$. It gives the exact sequence $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\xrightarrow{\delta} E\to\Omega_{L/k}\to0$, where $\delta(b\bmod\mathfrak m^2)=db\otimes1$. The finite separable hypothesis on $L/k$ gives $\Omega_{L/k}=0$ by [lem-trf-separable-field-differentials-vanish]. Exactness therefore makes $\delta$ surjective. Since $d\geq1$, the vector $(1,0,\ldots,0)\in L^d$ is nonzero. Pull it back through the isomorphism of Step 4 to a nonzero $v\in E$, choose a class in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ mapping to $v$, and choose its representative $\bar h\in\mathfrak m$. Then $d\bar h\otimes1=v\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 057D, lemma-slice-smooth-once, proof, conormal sequence and choice of the germ; Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, positive-dimensional case; algebra.tex Tags 00RU and 090W.

proof.text: Use the surjection of [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] to lift $\bar h$ to $h\in T$. The equality $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x/J$ from Step 2 implies $h\in\mathfrak m_x$. The compatibility computed in Step 4 says that the image of $dh$ in the relative differential fibre is $d\bar h\otimes1$, hence is nonzero. In particular $\bar h\ne0$, since the differential of zero is zero. Finally, in the domain $R$ established in Step 3, $\bar h r=\bar h r'$ implies $\bar h(r-r')=0$, and therefore $r=r'$. Thus multiplication by $\bar h$ is injective, completing all assertions.

source.place: Tag 057D, lemma-slice-smooth-once, proof, last sentence (lifting); algebra.tex Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain, used in Step 3.
